rows.w: Gate-free 20-acre I-Drive entertainment hub anchored by The Wheel, a 400-ft observation wheel (opened 2015 as the Orlando Eye) with 50-mile views on clear days, plus the 450-ft StarFlyer and SlingShot.

SeaWorld's flagship marine park (1973) — Mako, Kraken, Manta, Pipeline and Penguin Trek coasters plus orca, dolphin and penguin habitats; the anchor of the I-Drive/SeaWorld district (Wikipedia; SeaWorld official).
Floorless B&M coaster with a 153-ft peak and 4,177 ft of track.
The first new stand-up coaster in 20+ years (2023).
SeaWorld's South Pacific-themed water park (opened 2008) mixing slides with animal habitats; Visit Orlando spotlights its Ray Rush raft slide.

Orlando's largest midway-style park (15 acres) at the top of I-Drive per Frommer's, with the Freedom Flyer suspended family coaster; Orlando Informer recommends it as the lower-key, cheaper alternative to the big parks.
Upside-down "sinking" building with upended palm trees outside and ~100 interactive science and VR experiences inside; a Fodor's best sight on International Drive.
Intamin river-rapids ride (opened Oct 2018) that holds the record for the tallest drop on a river rapids ride; centrepiece of SeaWorld's Sea of Fun area (Wikipedia; SeaWorld official).

Launched family coaster (2024) that replaced Antarctica: Empire of the Penguin — snowmobile cars at up to 43 mph ending at a real penguin habitat in the Sea of Ice area (Wikipedia; SeaWorld official).

rows.w: Downtown's oldest building (1886) — a Queen Anne-style English gentlemen's club built by Gordon Rogers, NRHP 1983; donated to the city in 2018 as the Rogers-Kiene Building and home to CityArts' seven galleries (Clio; Visit Orlando; Orlando Weekly).
College Park cottage where Kerouac wrote The Dharma Bums (1957–58); now a writers' residency.
1889 railroad depot with a conical tower at the heart of the Church Street bar-and-restaurant district.
John Johansen's 1966 Brutalist library; a corner upstairs holds the Disney Collection of park history (Atlas Obscura).
"The jewel of downtown Orlando": Joseph Ange's 11-storey 1923 Angebilt Hotel by Murry S. King — rooftop garden, WLOF radio on the mezzanine; NRHP-listed (Wikipedia; CRA historical marker).

One of Orlando's oldest, most architecturally mixed neighbourhoods — ~500 historic bungalows, Colonial Revivals and Queen Annes on brick streets above Lake Eola; NRHP 1992 and a city historic preservation district (Wikipedia; City of Orlando).
1893 Queen Anne house on Lake Lucerne, now a B&B (NRHP).

1925 glazed-brick-and-terracotta commercial building put up for $90,000 by Hall of Fame Cubs shortstop Joe Tinker for his real-estate office; NRHP 1980; later housed the Orlando Magic's and Orlando Weekly's offices (City of Orlando walking tour; NRHP nomination).

Postmodern 1991 city hall whose 1958 predecessor next door was imploded on 24 Oct 1991 for the opening scene of Lethal Weapon 3; the rotunda hosts the Terrace Gallery art shows (City of Orlando; ORL Today).

Voted Best Downtown Restaurant and Best Brunch in Orlando Weekly's Best of Orlando 2026 readers' poll, and a MICHELIN Guide-listed Colonialtown neighborhood bistro. Order: Fried green tomatoes with crab cakes.

Voted Best College Park Restaurant in Orlando Weekly's Best of Orlando 2026 readers' poll; the clubhouse grill at the historic Dubsdread golf course, famed for its half-pound burger (Tasty Chomps). Order: Tap Room classic cheeseburger.

Won Best Bagel Shop in Orlando Weekly's 2026 Best of Orlando readers' poll; WFTV covered its growth from a Winter Garden home bakery to a local chain (College Park shop listed). Order: New York-style bagel.

MICHELIN Bib Gourmand (Florida guide): lakeside dining room over Lake Ivanhoe named for Orlando's pineapple-growing past; Michelin singles out the smoked peanut soup and pimento-cheese bread board. Visit Orlando Michelin roundup also lists it in Ivanhoe Village. Order: Smoked peanut soup; bread board with pimento cheese.

Parramore's living landmark: opened 1949 as Roser's Restaurant, it fed chitlin'-circuit musicians, athletes and civil-rights leaders; renamed Nikki's Place in 1999 and reopened in 2017 after a 2015 fire with city grants. Orlando Weekly calls it one of Orlando's most distinctive meat-and-threes; Scott Joseph reviewed it on WMFE. Order: Meat-and-three: oxtails, chitterlings, fried pork chops, catfish.

Creative Village comfort-food restaurant named for Wells'Built founder Dr. William Monroe Wells; Orlando Weekly named it a best opening of 2021 and voted it #3 Best Downtown Restaurant in Best of Orlando 2025, and The Infatuation recommends its fried chicken.

Ivanhoe Village's 30-plus-year 'Orlando Classic' (Scott Joseph) — an antique shop turned cafe-bar, named for the owners' white shepherd; Orlando Weekly readers' #2 Ivanhoe Village restaurant 2025; Food Network's $40 a Day stop; Tasty Chomps snapshots. Order: giant cinnamon rolls, weekend brunch among antiques.

Downtown chophouse in a 1930s Church Street landmark, reviewed by Orlando Weekly and Scott Joseph and voted #2 Best Downtown Restaurant in Orlando Weekly's Best of Orlando 2025. Order: House-aged prime steak.

Thornton Park's polished-casual New American restaurant & wine bar (since 2012, repeat Wine Spectator Award of Excellence); moved from College Park to Thornton Park in 2021 (News 6); Visit Orlando listing. Order: new American plates with a Wine Spectator-awarded list.

College Park's breakfast-and-lunch diner (since the 1990s) named for its salt-and-pepper-shaker collection — Scott Joseph 'bona fide Orlando Classic' and Foodster Best Breakfast 2017; Orlando Weekly Edgewater essential + Best of Orlando 2026 entry. Order: breakfast plates and daily quiche under a wall of salt-and-pepper shakers.

Durable Thornton Park New American restaurant in the Sanctuary building, reviewed by Scott Joseph and voted #2 Best Thornton Park/South Eola Restaurant in Orlando Weekly's Best of Orlando 2025. Order: Moscow Mule in a copper cup.

Thornton Park's 80-plus-year neighbourhood bar — one of downtown's longest-lived establishments, reopened under the same name in 2017 by The Lodge/The Woods owners; Orlando Weekly: the area's 'cheapest and friendliest' with a prime people-watching patio. Order: neighbourhood-bar burgers and cheap drinks on the patio.
